hero.name: Lefteris Evangelinos

featuredProjects.title: Featured Projects
featuredProjects.note: Note: Due to confidentiality agreements with clients and employers, not all projects I've contributed to can be publicly shared. The projects showcased here represent a selection of my publicly available work that demonstrates my technical capabilities and approach to problem-solving.

contactCTA.title: Let's Build Something Together
contactCTA.description: I'm always interested in hearing about new projects and opportunities. Whether you have a question or just want to say hi, feel free to reach out.

whoIAm.title: Who I Am
whoIAm.content: I'm Lefteris Evangelinos, a full-stack developer and software engineer with a passion for building scalable systems and crafting immersive stories. Born in Volos, Greece, with roots in Lavkos and Argalasti in South Pelion, I've always been drawn to both the technical precision of code and the creative freedom of storytelling.
whoIAm.education: I studied Computer Engineering at the University of West Attica, where I developed a strong foundation in software architecture, database design, and modern web technologies. My professional work focuses on backend development with Node.js and Express, real-time systems with Socket.IO, and creating intuitive user experiences with Vue.js and TypeScript.
whoIAm.philosophy: Core Philosophy: Whether I'm architecting a backend API or developing a fantasy world, I believe in attention to detail, clear structure, and the power of well-crafted systems to create meaningful experiences.

technicalJourney.title: Technical Journey
technicalJourney.description: My development work spans multiple domains, from carpooling platforms with multi-language support and real-time chat to multiplayer game applications with comprehensive admin dashboards. I'm particularly interested in:
interests: Backend Architecture: Building RESTful APIs, managing complex data flows, and ensuring system reliability through proper error handling and validation.
Real-time Systems: Implementing WebSocket communications, managing concurrent users, and creating responsive live experiences.
Modern Frontend: Crafting type-safe interfaces with Vue 3 and TypeScript, managing application state, and creating accessible user experiences.
DevOps & Automation: Writing deployment scripts, managing environments, and building tools that streamline development workflows.
technicalJourney.approach: I approach every project as an opportunity to learn and refine my craft. From authentication flows and session management to notification systems and scheduled jobs, I'm constantly exploring ways to make systems more robust, maintainable, and user-friendly.

literaryWork.title: Literary Work
literaryWork.description: Beyond the world of code, I'm a published fantasy author with a deep love for epic storytelling. Since childhood, I've been captivated by fantasy literature—works by Robert Jordan and Tolkien shaped my imagination and inspired me to create my own fantastical worlds.
literaryWork.content: Through my writing, I explore themes that matter in the real world, weaving my concerns, thoughts, and reflections into narratives that blend heroic adventure with philosophical depth. My stories are not just escapism; they're a mirror reflecting the complexities of our world through the lens of fantasy.

publishedWorks.title: Published Works
publishedWorks.description: My main series, "Το πεπρωμένο του Ραθ" (The Fate of Rath), is an epic fantasy trilogy published by Συμπαντικές Διαδρομές (Universe Pathways Editions). The series concluded with the release of the third book at the "Όψεις του Φανταστικού" (Aspects of the Fantastic) festival.

otherPublications.title: Other Publications
otherPublications.description: In addition to my main series, I've contributed to several anthology collections and collaborative projects in the Greek fantasy community:
publications: Πεφταστέρι – Poetry and short prose collection (4.78/5 rating)
Larry Niven 2021 & 2022 – Fantasy literature award collections
Θρύλοι του Σύμπαντος X – Collaborative anthology
Contributions to "There Once Was A Myth", "Echoes of a Lost Time", and "The Path Not Taken"

influences.literary: Brandon Sanderson, Robert Jordan, J.R.R. Tolkien
influences.themes: Fate vs. free will, redemption, the cost of power, philosophical reflection

publishedWorks.goodreads: I maintain an active presence on Goodreads, where I engage with the fantasy community, share reviews, and connect with fellow readers and writers. My current reading challenge for 2025 aims for 30 books, and I'm particularly enjoying Brandon Sanderson's Stormlight Archive series.

bringingItTogether.title: Bringing It All Together
bringingItTogether.content: My dual passions for software development and storytelling inform each other in unexpected ways. The systematic thinking required for coding helps me structure complex narratives, while the creative freedom of writing keeps my problem-solving fresh and innovative.
bringingItTogether.approach: Whether I'm debugging a WebSocket connection or developing a character arc, I approach each challenge with curiosity, discipline, and a commitment to craft. Both fields demand attention to detail, an understanding of structure, and the ability to create systems—whether they're software architectures or fictional worlds—that feel cohesive and alive.
bringingItTogether.invitation: If you'd like to discuss technology, collaborate on a project, or talk about fantasy literature, I'd love to hear from you. Let's create something remarkable together.

posts.title: Markdown Style Guide
posts.description: Here is a sample of some basic Markdown syntax that can be used when writing Markdown content in Astro.
posts.content:
Here is a sample of some basic Markdown syntax that can be used when writing Markdown content in Astro. ## Headings The following HTML `

`—`

` elements represent six levels of section headings. `

` is the highest section level while `

` is the lowest. # H1 ## H2 ### H3 #### H4 ##### H5 ###### H6 ## Paragraph Xerum, quo qui aut unt expliquam qui dolut labo. Aque venitatiusda cum, voluptionse latur sitiae dolessi aut parist aut dollo enim qui voluptate ma dolestendit peritin re plis aut quas inctum laceat est volestemque commosa as cus endigna tectur, offic to cor sequas etum rerum idem sintibus eiur? Quianimin porecus evelectur, cum que nis nust voloribus ratem aut omnimi, sitatur? Quiatem. Nam, omnis sum am facea corem alique molestrunt et eos evelece arcillit ut aut eos eos nus, sin conecerem erum fuga. Ri oditatquam, ad quibus unda veliamenimin cusam et facea ipsamus es exerum sitate dolores editium rerore eost, temped molorro ratiae volorro te reribus dolorer sperchicium faceata tiustia prat. Itatur? Quiatae cullecum rem ent aut odis in re eossequodi nonsequ idebis ne sapicia is sinveli squiatum, core et que aut hariosam ex eat. ## Images ### Syntax ```markdown ![Alt text](./full/or/relative/path/of/image) ``` ### Output ![blog placeholder](../../assets/blog-placeholder-about.jpg) ## Blockquotes The blockquote element represents content that is quoted from another source, optionally with a citation which must be within a `footer` or `cite` element, and optionally with in-line changes such as annotations and abbreviations. ### Blockquote without attribution #### Syntax ```markdown > Tiam, ad mint andaepu dandae nostion secatur sequo quae. > **Note** that you can use _Markdown syntax_ within a blockquote. ``` #### Output > Tiam, ad mint andaepu dandae nostion secatur sequo quae. > **Note** that you can use _Markdown syntax_ within a blockquote. ### Blockquote with attribution #### Syntax ```markdown > Don't communicate by sharing memory, share memory by communicating.
> — Rob Pike[^1] ``` #### Output > Don't communicate by sharing memory, share memory by communicating.
> — Rob Pike[^1] [^1]: The above quote is excerpted from Rob Pike's [talk](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PAAkCSZUG1c) during Gopherfest, November 18, 2015. ## Tables ### Syntax ```markdown | Italics | Bold | Code | | --------- | -------- | ------ | | _italics_ | **bold** | `code` | ``` ### Output | Italics | Bold | Code | | --------- | -------- | ------ | | _italics_ | **bold** | `code` | ## Code Blocks ### Syntax we can use 3 backticks ``` in new line and write snippet and close with 3 backticks on new line and to highlight language specific syntax, write one word of language name after first 3 backticks, for eg. html, javascript, css, markdown, typescript, txt, bash ````markdown ```html Example HTML5 Document

Test

``` ```` ### Output ```html Example HTML5 Document

Test

``` ## List Types ### Ordered List #### Syntax ```markdown 1. First item 2. Second item 3. Third item ``` #### Output 1. First item 2. Second item 3. Third item ### Unordered List #### Syntax ```markdown - List item - Another item - And another item ``` #### Output - List item - Another item - And another item ### Nested list #### Syntax ```markdown - Fruit - Apple - Orange - Banana - Dairy - Milk - Cheese ``` #### Output - Fruit - Apple - Orange - Banana - Dairy - Milk - Cheese ## Other Elements — abbr, sub, sup, kbd, mark ### Syntax ```markdown GIF is a bitmap image format. H2O Xn + Yn = Zn Press CTRL + ALT + Delete to end the session. Most salamanders are nocturnal, and hunt for insects, worms, and other small creatures. ``` ### Output GIF is a bitmap image format. H2O Xn + Yn = Zn Press CTRL + ALT + Delete to end the session. Most salamanders are nocturnal, and hunt for insects, worms, and other small creatures.

posts.title: Using MDX
posts.content: This theme comes with the [@astrojs/mdx](https://docs.astro.build/en/guides/integrations-guide/mdx/) integration installed and configured in your `astro.config.mjs` config file. If you prefer not to use MDX, you can disable support by removing the integration from your config file. ## Why MDX? MDX is a special flavor of Markdown that supports embedded JavaScript & JSX syntax. This unlocks the ability to [mix JavaScript and UI Components into your Markdown content](https://docs.astro.build/en/guides/markdown-content/#mdx-features) for things like interactive charts or alerts. If you have existing content authored in MDX, this integration will hopefully make migrating to Astro a breeze. ## Example Here is how you import and use a UI component inside of MDX.   When you open this page in the browser, you should see the clickable button below. import HeaderLink from '../../components/HeaderLink.astro'; <HeaderLink href="#" onclick="alert('clicked!')"> Embedded component in MDX </HeaderLink> ## More Links - [MDX Syntax Documentation](https://mdxjs.com/docs/what-is-mdx) - [Astro Usage Documentation](https://docs.astro.build/en/guides/markdown-content/#markdown-and-mdx-pages) - **Note:** [Client Directives](https://docs.astro.build/en/reference/directives-reference/#client-directives) are still required to create interactive components. Otherwise, all components in your MDX will render as static HTML (no JavaScript) by default.

nestjs-backend-template.title: NestJS Backend Template
nestjs-backend-template.description: A robust, production-ready NestJS template that emphasizes clean architecture, security, and developer experience. Out of the box you get JWT authentication, Swagger documentation, structured logging, Prometheus metrics, and comprehensive error tracking.

highlights.title: Security First
highlights.content: JWT authentication, Helmet security headers, CORS configuration, rate limiting, and validated environment configuration protect every endpoint from day one.

highlights.title: Observable
highlights.content: Structured Pino logging, Kubernetes-ready health probes, Prometheus metrics, and Sentry error tracking give teams complete visibility into service behavior.

highlights.title: Developer Ready
highlights.content: Interactive Swagger documentation, pre-configured linting with Husky hooks, REST Client collections, and TypeScript strict mode make iteration fast and safe.

nestjs-backend-template.whatIBuilt: I created a comprehensive NestJS template that serves as a solid foundation for any backend service. It removes the boilerplate of setting up authentication, observability, security, and documentation so teams can focus on business logic from day one. The template emphasizes sensible defaults and production-grade patterns.
features: JWT-based authentication with guards and utilities for protected routes.
Interactive Swagger/OpenAPI documentation at /api-docs with schema validation.
Kubernetes-ready health checks: comprehensive, liveness, and readiness probes.
Prometheus-compatible metrics endpoint for monitoring and alerting.
Structured JSON logging with Pino for high-performance observability.
Sentry integration for production error tracking and alerting.
Pre-commit hooks with Husky for automated linting and formatting.
Global validation pipes with class-validator for consistent request validation.
URI-based API versioning for backward-compatible evolution.
Security hardening with Helmet, CORS, and rate limiting configured.
nestjs-backend-template.architecture: The template follows NestJS module architecture with clear separation of concerns. Authentication logic lives in dedicated guards and decorators, configuration validation happens at startup with class-validator, and middleware layers handle security, logging, and error transformation consistently across all endpoints.

stack.core: NestJS, TypeScript (strict mode), Node.js 16+, Express adapter
stack.security: JWT, Helmet, CORS, Rate limiting, class-validator, Global exception filters
stack.observability: Pino structured logging, Prometheus metrics, Health checks (Terminus), Sentry error tracking, Swagger/OpenAPI documentation

nestjs-backend-template.devExperience: The template ships with comprehensive tooling for developer productivity. Husky pre-commit hooks automatically lint and format code before commits, preventing style drift. REST Client files and Postman collections let developers test endpoints without leaving their editor. TypeScript strict mode catches issues at compile time, and Swagger documentation stays in sync with code through decorators.
nestjs-backend-template.outcome: This template has been battle-tested across multiple projects and provides a strong foundation for building production services. It eliminates weeks of setup time, enforces best practices through automation, and gives teams immediate visibility into service health. The modular structure makes it easy to extend while maintaining consistency.
nestjs-backend-template.cta: Check out the template, read the comprehensive documentation, or use it as a starting point for your next backend service.

share-the-ride.title: Share the Ride Backend
share-the-ride.description: Share is the production-ready Node.js and Express service behind the "Share the Ride" carpooling platform, delivering secure REST and WebSocket experiences for riders and drivers.

highlights.title: Production Ready
highlights.content: Multi-region deployments with environment-aware configuration, rate limiting, and zero-downtime releases keep commuter traffic flowing.

highlights.title: Secure by Design
highlights.content: Tenant-aware JWT flows, audit trails, and encryption utilities give riders and drivers credible trust guarantees.

highlights.title: Observability
highlights.content: Centralized logging, Grafana dashboards, and synthetic health probes surface issues long before users notice.

share-the-ride.whatIBuilt: I designed and implemented a layered backend that keeps the platform reliable and responsive. It orchestrates authentication, ride workflows, chat, notifications, and scheduled maintenance jobs while staying adaptable to feature requests from product and mobile teams.
features: JWT-secured APIs covering posts, interests, reviews, and rider onboarding.
Real-time Socket.IO messaging with optional AES encryption and Firebase fallback alerts.
Daily jobs that archive stale posts, refresh ride statistics, and prune expired conversations.
share-the-ride.architecture: The service follows a clear separation of concerns: Express routers feed thin controllers, business logic lives in domain services, and Sequelize modules handle data access for MySQL. Shared utilities cover localization, notifications, and encryption so each feature team has consistent building blocks.

stack.messagingAuth: JWT, Firebase Cloud Messaging, Redis (optional), Nodemailer
stack.operational: node-schedule jobs, Docker-ready configuration, REST client collections

share-the-ride.outcome: Share has supported multi-language trip planning across web and mobile clients since launch. The backend scales comfortably on Node 16+, keeps ride data fresh with automated pruning, and provides a single source of truth for notifications and chat history.
share-the-ride.cta: Interested in the technical deep dive or API coverage? Let's chat about the architecture decisions and how they can translate to your next mobility project.

ert-game-web.title: Web game
ert-game-web.description: A real-time multiplayer game platform where players submit answers, vote on responses, and compete for points. Built with Express.js, Vue 3, TypeScript, and featuring comprehensive admin controls and session management.

highlights.title: Party Ready
highlights.content: Sessions spin up in seconds with QR join codes, responsive layouts, and soundtrack support for a couch-friendly trivia experience.

highlights.title: Host Controls
highlights.content: Admins orchestrate rounds, tweak scoring, and broadcast announcements with guardrails for multiplayer fairness.

highlights.title: Analytics
highlights.content: Game exports and dashboards track engagement, highlight best answers, and inform future content drops.

ert-game-web.whatIBuilt: Web Game is a complete full-stack application that demonstrates modern web development practices. The platform supports multiple players simultaneously, real-time game state management, and provides both player and administrator interfaces with distinct workflows.
features: Real-time multiplayer gameplay with round-based question-answer mechanics.
Dual-interface design: streamlined player view and comprehensive admin dashboard.
Session management with voting system, point tracking, and game history exports.
Automated installation scripts for Windows (PowerShell) and Linux/macOS (Bash).
RESTful API with health checks, CORS configuration, and proper error handling.
ert-game-web.architecture: The backend runs on Express.js with JSON file-based persistence for session data and round status. The Vue 3 frontend leverages TypeScript, Pinia state management, and modern Sass modules for styling. Component organization follows domain-driven principles, separating player, admin, and shared UI elements.

stack.backend: Node.js, Express, RESTful APIs, JSON persistence
stack.frontend: Vue 3, TypeScript, Vite, Pinia, Sass modules
stack.devops: Automated installers, environment detection, health checks

ert-game-web.apiHighlights: The server exposes comprehensive endpoints for session management, round status tracking, and player operations including joining, answering, voting, and point updates. All routes return consistent JSON responses with proper HTTP status codes.
ert-game-web.outcome: The application has been deployed and tested across different environments. The installer scripts detect IP addresses automatically and configure both server and client for immediate use. The architecture scales comfortably for local network gameplay and supports export functionality for game analytics.
ert-game-web.cta: Explore the repository, check out the component architecture, or run the game locally.

python-random-scripts.title: Python Random Scripts
python-random-scripts.description: A living collection of small Python utilities where I explore everyday automation, quick data experiments, and CLI helpers. Each script solves a specific problem and doubles as a playground for sharpening language features and third-party packages.

highlights.title: Automation
highlights.content: From renaming media libraries to posting daily digests, these jobs showcase how cron-friendly Python scripts tame repetitive work.

highlights.title: Data Experiments
highlights.content: Lightweight notebooks and CLI parsers that clean CSV batches, reshape JSON, and visualize quick stats with pandas and Rich.

seo-optimizer.title: SEO Optimizer
seo-optimizer.description: A standalone desktop SEO analysis and optimization tool built with Electron, React, and SQLite. Features comprehensive SEO analysis engine with 13 rules, 17 mini-services for keyword analysis, readability scoring, and content optimization.

highlights.title: Comprehensive Analysis
highlights.content: 13 SEO rules across 4 categories (meta, content, technical, readability) with weighted scoring system and letter grade assessment (A-F) for actionable insights.

highlights.title: 17 Mini-Services
highlights.content: Keyword services (density, long-tail generation, difficulty estimation, clustering, LSI), readability services (multi-formula scoring, improvement suggestions), and content optimization tools (structure analysis, link recommendations).

highlights.title: Desktop Application
highlights.content: Standalone Electron app with React frontend, SQLite database, secure IPC communication, and dark theme UI. Works offline with local data storage.

seo-optimizer.whatIBuilt: I built a complete desktop SEO analysis tool that provides comprehensive on-page SEO auditing and optimization recommendations. The application combines multiple analysis engines into a unified interface, making it easy for content creators and SEO professionals to evaluate and improve their web content. Note: This project was an experimental implementation using AI-assisted coding techniques with minimal code review, serving as a learning exercise in rapid prototyping and exploring modern development workflows.
features: SEO analysis engine with 13 rules across meta tags, content quality, technical SEO, and readability.
Weighted scoring system (0-100%) with letter grade assessment (A-F) and detailed issue reporting.
Keyword density analyzer with real-time visualization and density tracking.
Long-tail keyword generator for discovering low-competition opportunities.
Keyword difficulty estimator and clustering tools for competitive analysis.
LSI keyword generator for finding semantically related terms.
Readability analysis with multiple formulas (Flesch Reading Ease, etc.) and grade level assessment.
Content structure analyzer for headings, paragraphs, lists, and media optimization.
Internal link recommender with anchor text analysis.
Content length optimizer with type-specific recommendations.
Content gap analyzer for topic coverage and depth analysis.
Competitive content analyzer to compare against top-ranking pages.
Multi-language support (English & Greek) with language-specific readability rules.
SQLite database for storing analysis history and reports.
Secure Electron architecture with context isolation and secure IPC communication.
seo-optimizer.architecture: The application follows a three-process Electron architecture: main process handles database operations and SEO analysis logic, renderer process contains the React UI with component-based architecture, and preload script provides secure IPC bridge. The SEO analyzer module contains all analysis engines, while mini-services are organized into keyword, readability, and content optimization categories. SQLite stores analysis history and reports locally.

stack.frontend: React with SASS modules, dark theme UI, component-based architecture
stack.backend: Node.js, Electron main process, SQLite database, IPC handlers, SEO analyzer engine, HTML parser, keyword services, readability services, content services

seo-optimizer.devExperience: The project includes comprehensive development tooling with webpack for bundling main, preload, and renderer processes separately. TypeScript strict mode ensures type safety, ESLint and Prettier maintain code quality, and Husky pre-commit hooks automate quality checks. The modular architecture allows easy extension of analysis rules and services.
seo-optimizer.outcome: SEO Optimizer provides a complete desktop solution for SEO analysis without requiring internet connectivity or external services. The 17 mini-services cover the full spectrum of on-page SEO optimization, from keyword research to content structure analysis. The application has been refactored to use standardized component patterns, reducing boilerplate code by approximately 25-30% while maintaining all functionality.
seo-optimizer.cta: Explore the repository, check out the comprehensive documentation, or use it to analyze and optimize your web content.
